cliffs.title: CUDA 13.0 drops offline compilation + library support for pre-Turing
cliffs.breaks: CUDA Toolkit 13.0 removes OFFLINE COMPILATION and library (cuFFT, etc.) support for architectures below compute capability 7.5 (Maxwell sm_50/52, Pascal sm_60/61, Volta sm_70). nvcc in 13.x can no longer target these archs; 12.x toolkits can still build for them.
cliffs.fix: Pin CUDA Toolkit 12.9 (the last toolkit that can target sm_50-sm_72) and use driver branch R580. Build frameworks against cu12.x, not cu13.
cliffs.source_note: NVIDIA dev blog + CUDA Features Archive: "Architecture support for Maxwell, Pascal, and Volta is considered feature-complete ... offline compilation and library support for these architectures have been removed in CUDA Toolkit 13.0." Runtime execution via the R580 driver is unaffected.

cliffs.title: R580 is the last NVIDIA driver branch for pre-CC-7.5 GPUs
cliffs.breaks: Driver branch 580 is the final branch to support GPUs before compute capability 7.5. Branches after 580 ship open-kernel ("open-only") modules that do not cover Maxwell/Pascal/Volta, so those cards lose driver support.
cliffs.fix: Stay on the R580 driver branch (580.xx; 580.173.02 is the build 1Cat-vLLM tested for sm_70). NVIDIA states R580 supports these GPUs through mid-year 2028. Do not upgrade past the 580 branch.
cliffs.source_note: NVIDIA dev blog: "This will be the final branch that supports GPUs before CC 7.5 ... supported until mid-year 2028." Branch number 590 is used here as the first-breaking sentinel (anything newer than the 580 branch).

cliffs.title: PyTorch 2.15 drops cu126 wheels for Maxwell/Pascal/Volta
cliffs.breaks: PyTorch 2.14 is the last release to ship any CUDA 12.x (cu126) prebuilt wheels. From 2.15, CUDA 12.6 is build-from-source only, so `pip install torch` 2.15+ carries no kernels for sm_50/60/70 and fails with an unsupported-arch / "no kernel image is available" error on these cards.
cliffs.fix: Pin `torch==2.14.0` installed from the cu126 index (--index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu126), or build torch from source against CUDA 12.x for these archs.
cliffs.source_note: PyTorch dev-discuss: "PyTorch 2.14 is the last release to ship any CUDA 12.x wheels"; "PyTorch will stop publishing CUDA 12.6 binaries in 2.15." Maxwell sm_50 / Pascal sm_60 / Volta sm_70 listed as dropped.

cliffs.title: vLLM deprecated V100 / sm_70 (V0 engine removal, v0.10, Jul 2025)
cliffs.breaks: vLLM's V0-engine deprecation (announced v0.10.0, 2025-07-01; V0 code fully removed ~v0.11.0, Aug 2025) lists "V100 support" under features permanently dropped. Stock latest vLLM refuses / lacks tuned kernels for sm_70 on the V1 engine for many models.
cliffs.fix: Use the community 1Cat-vLLM SM70 fork + wheel (credit upstream 1CatAI), or pin vLLM <= 0.9.x. Evaluate the V1-engine path per model, since some V1 paths may still run on older GPUs after PR #24022.
cliffs.source_note: Issue #18571 lists "V100 support" under "Features Permanently Dropped" and dates v0.10.0 to 2025-07-01, but it does NOT name sm_70 and does NOT tie the V100 drop to a specific version; maintainers later commented V1 "should be supported already" on older GPUs. Exact removal version is nuanced -- treat as a deprecation direction, not a hard version cutoff.

cliffs.title: ROCm 7.x lists gfx900/gfx906 (Vega/MI50) as unsupported
cliffs.breaks: ROCm 7.0+ Linux system-requirements tables mark MI50/Radeon VII/Radeon PRO VII (gfx906) and MI25 (gfx900) with an explicit NOT-supported mark. Prebuilt ROCm libraries are not official for these cards; HIP may still run but library kernels can error at runtime.
cliffs.fix: For gfx906, use TheRock 7.x nightly community builds (credit TheRock), or ROCm 6.4.x with restored gfx906 Tensile/rocBLAS logic files, plus a llama.cpp HIP build and a Vulkan fallback. ROCm 5.7 was the last fully supported release for gfx906.
cliffs.source_note: ROCm 7.0.0 (and 7.2.x) Linux system-requirements tables show MI50 (gfx906) and MI25 (gfx900) unsupported; already unsupported in 6.4.x tables. gfx906 entered maintenance mode in ROCm 6.0; 5.7 was last fully supported.

cliffs.title: ROCm 6.4 stopped shipping gfx906 Tensile kernels (UNVERIFIED)
cliffs.breaks: Reported: ROCm 6.4 stopped shipping prebuilt gfx906 Tensile logic files, so rocBLAS GEMM has no tuned gfx906 kernels and falls back / errors. This is what makes MI50 need restored Tensile files on 6.4.x.
cliffs.fix: Use ROCm 6.4.x with gfx906 Tensile/rocBLAS logic files restored from a community build (e.g. mixa3607/ML-gfx906, credit upstream), or prefer TheRock 7.x nightly / a Vulkan fallback.
cliffs.source_note: Could NOT confirm from AMD primary docs on 2026-11-06. ROCm 6.4.3 notes list Tensile 4.43.0 / rocBLAS 4.4.1 without mentioning gfx906 logic-file removal. Only third-party leads (mixa3607 "rocm-tensile marked as deprecated"). gfx906 deprecation pre-6.4 IS documented (maint. since 6.0).

cliffs.title: Ollama 0.13.0 dropped gfx906 (UNVERIFIED -- not in release notes)
cliffs.breaks: Claimed: Ollama 0.13.0 dropped gfx906 (Radeon VII / MI50) from its ROCm build targets, so stock Ollama no longer detects the card and skips it.
cliffs.fix: Run Ollama with the Vulkan backend (OLLAMA_VULKAN=1) as a fallback, pin Ollama <= 0.12.x, or use a community AMD fork (e.g. ollama-for-amd) that still ships gfx906.
cliffs.source_note: Could NOT confirm on 2026-11-06. The v0.13.0 release notes mention only "Improved VRAM information detection for AMD GPUs" and a Vulkan library fix -- NO statement about dropping gfx906. User reports note stock Ollama does not natively detect Radeon VII and suggest OLLAMA_VULKAN=1. Version 0.13.0 as the specific drop point is unconfirmed and may be inaccurate.

cliffs.title: FlashAttention-2 needs sm_80+ (Ampere); no Volta/Pascal kernels
cliffs.breaks: The official flash-attn (FlashAttention-2) package ships CUDA kernels only for compute capability 8.0+ (Ampere/Ada/Hopper). It uses Ampere+ MMA instructions, so Volta (sm_70), Pascal (sm_61) and earlier have no kernels; Turing (sm_75) is best-effort / historically "coming soon", not reliable.
cliffs.fix: Do not rely on flash-attn 2 on these cards. Use the Triton port `flash-attn-triton` (Turing-capable), xformers memory-efficient attention, or the framework's default (non-flash) attention. FlashAttention-3 targets Hopper only.
cliffs.source_note: FlashAttention README/notes: FA2 supports Ampere/Ada/Hopper (A100, RTX 3090/4090, H100); Volta unsupported (MMA requires >= Ampere, per FastAttention arXiv:2410.16663). Corroborated by multiple third-party sources; Turing status conflicts across sources -> flagged best-effort.
